featured_reviews.name: Prathamesh dalvi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Instagrammable Bandra café with average food and high prices 📸

Visited Juco Café around 2 PM for lunch. The café is quite small and a bit cramped with just about four tables, but I have to say — the ambience is super aesthetic, vibrant, and cozy. It’s one of those cute little spots that photograph really well and give off good vibes.

We ordered a few things to try:
🍜 Japanese Ramen Bowl (₹520) – The quantity was generous, and the flavours were quite nice. It’s a comforting bowl and filling enough for one person.
🍳 Shakshouka (₹400) – This one was surprisingly good! The taste was on point, and the portion size was enough for two people to share.
🥤 Blueberry Spirulina Smoothie (₹400) – Sadly, this was the only miss for us. It mostly tasted like banana with barely any blueberry flavour, so it didn’t feel worth the price.

The service was quite slow — it took about 35–40 minutes for our food to arrive, even though the café wasn’t crowded when we visited.

Overall, I’d give 3/5 stars. The pricing is definitely on the higher side, and while the food was decent, it’s not something I’d crave to go back for (except maybe to try their smoothie bowls next time!).

Had lunch at The Village Shop today with my husband and overall it was a good experience. The food was fresh, wholesome, and it’s definitely a great place for people with allergies, dietary restrictions, or specific food preferences.

There was one mix-up where potato was added instead of sweet potato mash in one of the dishes, but the team replaced it with exotic vegetables without any issue, which we appreciated.

featured_reviews.name: Neeraja Sundar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very ghastly and amusing experience at the Village Shop. I spent a Monday morning here, was hoping to get my coffee and breakfast  in some peace and quiet. It was only me in the cafe and the owner with 2 of her staff on another table.
In the first 10 mins I figured the owner had issues with staff, even though they spoke in hushed tones.

I let it slide. Naturally, I have no context of that conversation.
The food wasn’t up to the mark. They had it replaced without getting defensive.

Then, after a few mins I spoke loudly because I was on a call, and there was no one else in the cafe but me and the owner, I was asked to speak softly. She was irked. I gladly obliged.

I stepped outside to take my call. For 45 mins. In the heat. You see, I have been brought up with a lot of empathy.
It felt like my grandmother gave me a punishment to not enter the house.

What a ghastly experience for a Bandra cafe.  I hope the owners have the business acumen to start something else of their own. Customer centricity and empathy are not the strongest suit of some of the most affluent people in Bandra. What tarnishes reputation is lack of empathy for staff and no understanding of what customer focus looks like.

Money can’t buy you manners or class.

Its evident to me today, yet again :)

The café is listed as opening at 7:30 AM, and I’ve stopped by a few times around then after morning workouts. However, each time, the team has still been in the middle of setting up—cleaning, switching on machines—and not ready to serve even a simple coffee. If 7:30 AM is the stated opening time, it would be reasonable to expect at least basic service from then. Otherwise, it may be more accurate to list the opening time as 8:00 AM.

More importantly, on a couple of occasions, the person managing the morning shift (appears to be a lady dressed in black in a supervisory role) has responded in a rather abrupt and not very welcoming manner—almost as if customers are interrupting the opening process. It came across as dismissive, and at times borderline rude. This is what prompted me to finally write this.

My visit to Candies Café in Bandra was one of the most enjoyable and refreshing café experiences I’ve had in Mumbai. The moment you walk in, you’re greeted by a colourful, artistic, and lively atmosphere that feels warm, welcoming, and full of character. The café is known for its beautiful interiors, spacious seating, and charming décor that makes every corner picture-perfect. Whether you choose to sit indoors or enjoy the airy outdoor seating, the ambience makes you feel relaxed and comfortable.
Candies is famous for its wide variety of freshly prepared dishes—everything from sandwiches, rolls, and salads to desserts, pastries, and beverages. The best part is the display counter, which is filled with tempting options that make you want to try a little bit of everything. Their food tastes homemade, balanced, and full of flavour, making it perfect for both quick bites and long conversations. The desserts, especially the cakes and tarts, are a highlight and pair perfectly with their refreshing iced teas or hot beverages.
The café is always buzzing with people—students, professionals, families, and travellers—yet it never feels overwhelming because of its large, multi-section layout. The staff is polite, the service is fast, and the pricing is quite reasonable for the generous portions they offer.
What makes Candies truly special is the vibe. It’s more than just a café—it’s a place to unwind, meet friends, enjoy good food, and soak in the artistic charm of Bandra. Every visit feels memorable, and it’s easy to see why Candies is loved by so many.
